title: Phase Diagram of the Two-Dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Yu Duan, Hugues Chaté, Benoît Mahault, Xia-qing Shi
abstract: Motivated by gaps in our current knowledge of the Vicsek model, we present a major update of its phase diagram in two space dimensions, summarizing comprehensive numerical simulations at length- and timescales never explored before. Our main conclusions are that multiple phase separation scenarios are at play, not just the simple microphase separation put forward in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 114, 068101 (2015)], and that the coexistence phase is subdivided in two. We also map out the region of metastability of the homogeneous Toner-Tu liquid phase.
summary: This work provides a major revision of the phase diagram for the 2D Vicsek model, revealing complex phase separation regimes beyond simple predictions. By combining large-scale simulations with phenomenological theory, the authors successfully map out the metastability limit of the ordered liquid phase, highlighting the limitations of simple continuum theories in describing active matter dynamics.
main_problem: The paper updates the complex phase diagram of the two-dimensional Vicsek model and precisely maps the metastability limit of the ordered Toner-Tu liquid phase.
main_result: The phase diagram is more complex than previously thought, featuring multiple phase separation scenarios and a distinct metastability limit for the ordered liquid phase, which is derived both numerically and phenomenologically.
method: The authors combine extensive numerical simulations on large domains with the development and fitting of a phenomenological theory to analyze the growth speed of domain boundaries.
model_or_system: The system is the Vicsek model, a minimal model for collective motion of self-propelled particles whose alignment is governed by local interactions and rotational noise. The dynamics are described by continuous-time equations for particle positions and orientations.
key_observables: Phase diagram mapping, momentum field $\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{r})$, liquid fraction, band width, and the growth speed ($v_g$) of droplet fronts.
important_parameters: Global density ($ho_0$) and rotational noise strength ($D_r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing numerical results to a phenomenological theory derived for the growth speed, which is assumed to be valid except in regimes of strong fluctuations at low densities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the updated phase diagram in the $(	ext{density}, 	ext{noise strength})$ plane, showing multiple coexistence regions. Other figures detail the dynamics of domain growth, the linear dependence of the growth speed on noise, and the resulting metastability boundary.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first presenting the comprehensive numerical mapping of the phase diagram, then focusing on the complex coexistence region, and finally deriving and testing a phenomenological theory to pinpoint the metastability limit of the ordered liquid phase.
why_interesting: The study of Vicsek-type models provides a crucial non-equilibrium platform for studying collective dynamics, phase transitions, and pattern formation, which shares conceptual links with driven-dissipative quantum systems and active matter physics.
